About this view

A living relief of the commune and its vineyards, assembled from a navigable terrain model and mapped source layers.

RGE ALTI® · IGN BD TOPO® · INAO · DGFiP / Etalab
RHÔNE NORD / 2026 · Created by Daoyi ZhangCartographic boundaries are informative · source gaps documented in provenanceAbout & legal·

Atlas provenance

This atlas joins public terrain, land cover, buildings, roads and named place boundaries into a navigable commune scene.

Terrain
IGN RGE ALTI® 1 m ground terrain with 25 m overview and 200 m regional context terrain, sampled to the scene grid
Terroir figures
Slope, aspect and elevation range are computed from IGN RGE ALTI® terrain (1 m averaged to 5 m in Burgundy, 5 m in the Rhône). Direct sun hours are a clear-sky model with hill shading over 1 April–30 September, for comparing places, not a weather record.
Geology
BRGM BD Charm-50, harmonised 1:50,000 geological maps (Licence Ouverte 2.0), simplified to 2.5 m. Percentages are each formation’s share of the selected area. Surface deposits such as scree and colluvium are shown where they were mapped over the bedrock, and boundaries are good to a few tens of metres. English names and ages are translated from BRGM’s French legend.
Boundaries
INAO AOC appellation boundaries (the eight Northern Rhône crus and Côtes du Rhône), shown as informative overlays
Lieux-dits
DGFiP cadastral lieux-dits distributed by Cadastre Etalab (release 1 September 2026, Licence Ouverte 2.0), joined by name and shown where they touch an AOC area.
Landscape
IGN BD TOPO® buildings, roads and forest mask
Cadastral parcels
DGFiP cadastral data, transformed and distributed by Cadastre Etalab. Release: 1 September 2026. Licence Ouverte 2.0. Recorded cadastral area and calculated polygon area are shown separately; the release date is not an individual parcel survey date.

Display areas use one class at a time for clear viewing. Some source gaps remain across the regional index. Boundaries are informative and are not a legal survey.
